headline_marked: [[Googlebook]] now runs on Mac via unofficial virtual machine
headline: Googlebook now runs on Mac via unofficial virtual machine
summary: An open-source project allows Mac users to experience Google's new laptop OS without purchasing dedicated hardware.
details: An unofficial open-source project, gobs-vm, enables Mac users to run Google's new laptop OS via a virtual machine. This allows users to explore the software before committing to a purchase.

The project utilizes Google's recovery image for a Dell Googlebook, based on Android 17, ensuring an authentic experience. It replaces hardware-specific components with virtual alternatives and uses QEMU with GPU acceleration for graphics.
Users can experience browsing the internet on Google's new OS, as Chrome is confirmed to be working. The virtual machine runs non-intrusively, leaving Mac files and system settings untouched.

This solution is exclusively for Apple Silicon Macs and requires at least 16GB of RAM and 60GB of free storage, with a 9GB download for setup. Data is saved across sessions, and users can adjust resolution, memory, and CPU cores.

While not a perfect experience, gobs-vm provides a basic taste of Googlebook. Setting it up requires Xcode Command Line Tools, Homebrew, the Android SDK with NDK, and a Java Development Kit, though an installation script can assist.

The developer acknowledges limitations, stating not everything will function perfectly. However, for those curious about Googlebook without buying new hardware, this project offers a viable, albeit basic, preview.

headline_marked: Apple's [[OLED MacBook Pro]] to drive 50% surge in notebook display shipments
headline: Apple's OLED MacBook Pro to drive 50% surge in notebook display shipments
summary: Apple's next-gen MacBook Pro is expected to significantly boost OLED notebook display shipments, with a projected 50% increase in 2026 alone.
details: Counterpoint Research reports that Apple's upcoming OLED MacBook Pro models are poised to dramatically impact the premium display market.
The introduction of OLED technology in Apple's laptops is anticipated to fuel a substantial 50% rise in global OLED notebook display shipments within 2026.
This surge highlights a growing trend towards more advanced display technologies in portable computing, promising enhanced visuals and performance for users.
While specific launch dates remain unconfirmed, the anticipation for these OLED MacBooks is high, signaling a new era for Apple's premium laptop line.
